fatal_errors: The proposed carbon/low-alloy steel and chromium-segregation treatment do not reconstruct the AlCoCrFeNi-coated SS316L system or its 550 °C annealing intervention.
No prior findings or citations support the claimed beneficial effect of chromium segregation.

Chromium enrichment at boundaries is assumed to improve passivity without addressing adjacent chromium depletion, sensitization, secondary precipitates, or whether the alloy contains enough chromium to sustain a passive Cr-rich film.

Cooling and heat-treatment changes would alter grain size, precipitates, residual stress, and phase distribution as well as segregation, so the experiment does not isolate chromium segregation as the governing cause.
explanation: The response addresses corrosion resistance broadly and proposes measurable electrochemical outcomes, a uniform-composition baseline, microchemical characterization, and a clear null-result falsification rule. However, it is not a reconstruction of the target: it replaces SS316L bearing an atmospheric-plasma-sprayed AlCoCrFeNi coating with cast carbon/low-alloy steels, omits the coating and 550 °C annealing optimum, and tests chloride solution rather than sulfuric acid and cyclic molten-salt hot corrosion. The only substantive mechanistic overlap is chromium-rich passive-film formation. Even as an alternative hypothesis, evidence discipline is poor because no supporting findings are supplied and the central premise is chemically ambiguous: segregation may produce local enrichment but can also cause neighboring chromium depletion and intergranular corrosion. The proposed comparison is testable but insufficiently causal unless composition, grain size, precipitates, residual stress, and surface state are independently controlled.
